title: 1857 lost the war, and still ended Company rule
sources: NCERT Class 8, Our Pasts III, 'When People Rebel' (via BharatNotes study page)
Explainers on the revolt and its failure (GKToday; PW Only IAS)

quiz.q: What did the Government of India Act, 1858 do?
quiz.why: Right. The 1858 Act transferred the Company's powers, territories and revenues to the British Crown.

script: The revolt of 1857 was crushed.
The revolt of eighteen fifty-seven was crushed.
Yet it ended the East India Company's rule.
On 10 May 1857, sepoys at Meerut rose,
On the tenth of May, eighteen fifty-seven, sepoys at Meerut rose,
and marched to Delhi.
Rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal ruler, their emperor.
The trigger: new cartridges, reportedly greased with cow and pig fat.
Behind it: annexations, and long grievances.
Why did it fail?
It stayed mostly in the north and centre,
with no single plan or leader,
and many rulers sided with a better-armed British force.
In 1858, an Act of Parliament moved power from the Company to the Crown.
In eighteen fifty-eight, an Act of Parliament moved power from the Company to the Crown.
A lost revolt.
A changed Raj.
Your turn.
What did the Government of India Act, 1858 do?
What did the Government of India Act, eighteen fifty-eight do?

claims.claim: On 10 May 1857 sepoys at Meerut revolted and marched to Delhi (1857)
Rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal ruler, as their leader/emperor
The immediate trigger was the new Enfield cartridges, reportedly greased with cow and pig fat; annexations (e.g. Awadh, Doctrine of Lapse) were longer-term causes
Failure: confined mainly to north and central India; no unified leadership or plan; many rulers supported the British; superior British weapons and communications
The Government of India Act 1858 transferred the Company's powers, territories and revenues to the British Crown (1858)

review_note: Secondary sources only (NCERT-based study page and two explainers); check against NCERT Class 8 'When People Rebel' and Class 12 'Rebels and the Raj'. 'Reportedly' is kept for the cartridge grease, as NCERT presents it as the belief that spread. Left out: names of other leaders (Rani Lakshmibai, Nana Saheb, Tantia Tope, Kunwar Singh) for length; the 'First War of Independence' naming debate; casualty figures.
